Magical gene / spots and rings

Concentric Eyespots

Butterfly-wing eyespots - nested rings around a pale glinting core - scatter down the neck and all four legs.

Crossing two of them

Finding one

About 1 in 1,786 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Why it is built this way

Every band is a pair of SPOTS masks on ONE seed, spacing, stretch and vary, differing only in radius, with the smaller one subtracted out. That is what keeps the rings concentric AND in proportion: 'vary' scales every band of a given eyespot by the same per-cell factor, so a big one is a big one all the way through rather than a big rim round an average core.

The legs get three bands and the neck four. A leg is about four body units across and a texel is half a unit; a fourth band there would be under a texel wide and read as mush, so the leg version is deliberately simpler rather than every band being shrunk.

The rim and the core are fixed colours on both forms. They are the eyespot's structural dark edge and its glint, and they read as those whatever accent the horse carries - only the middle bands take the hue knob.

The band radii are wider than the import's by roughly double, and that is not taste. A texel is half a body unit; the original leg rings were 0.28 and 0.26 units from one edge to the next, so every band on every leg was under a texel wide and resolved to nothing at all. The import's own note said a FOURTH band would do that - it was already happening at three. Anything with structure inside it needs several units, and the spacing went up with the radii so the eyespots still do not touch.

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.
